vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: cellcog
Version: 2.0.11

The skill bundle describes an integration for an external AI service (cellcog.ai) that requires high-privilege access and security configuration changes. Specifically, SKILL.md instructs the agent or user to enable 'sessions_send' and 'sessions_list' in the OpenClaw gateway, which are disabled by default because they allow cross-session message injection. Additionally, the skill utilizes a background daemon for task monitoring and requests broad file system access via absolute paths for its '<SHOW_FILE>' functionality, creating a significant attack surface for data exfiltration or unauthorized system manipulation.

llm.summary: The skill's declared requirements and runtime instructions are coherent with an "any-input → any-output" AI client: it reasonably needs python3 and an API key and its prompts explain how to provide files and request outputs.

dimensions.detail: Name/description match what the SKILL.md does: it documents a Python SDK client that sends multi-modal inputs and requests multi-format outputs. Requiring python3 and CELLCOG_API_KEY is appropriate for this purpose; references to agent_provider and OpenClaw integration are explained and expected.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The instructions explicitly tell the agent how to include absolute file paths in <SHOW_FILE> tags so CellCog will read those files. That is consistent with the advertised multi-file capability, but it means anyone using the skill (or an agent given broad filesystem access) could send arbitrary local files to the remote service. The SKILL.md does not instruct the agent to read unrelated env vars or system configuration, but the file-read behavior is high-impact and requires user caution.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: This is instruction-only (no install spec). The doc suggests 'pip install cellcog' if import fails; that is a typical, user-initiated install path but carries usual pip risks (remote package code execution if the package or PyPI is malicious). No automatic download/install is specified by the skill itself.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Only CELLCOG_API_KEY is required, which matches an API-based client. The SKILL.md also uses an OpenClaw notify_session_key parameter (an agent session identifier) for notifications, which is expected for integration and not listed as a required environment variable. No unrelated credentials are requested.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill does not request always:true, does not install or modify agent configuration, and does not ask for elevated or persistent system privileges. Autonomous invocation is allowed by default (normal for skills) but the skill itself does not demand unusual persistence.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears coherent for its purpose, but take these precautions before installing or using it: 1) Treat CELLCOG_API_KEY like any secret API key—only provide it to trusted services and rotate it if compromised. 2) Be careful which local files you include with <SHOW_FILE> — any absolute path you pass can be uploaded to CellCog; do not expose secrets, keys, or private data unless you intend to send them. 3) The README suggests 'pip install cellcog' if needed; only install packages from trusted sources and verify the package name and publisher. 4) If you enable OpenClaw gateway sessions_send for notify_session_key delivery, understand that the gateway will receive/forward task notifications — review gateway settings and permissions. 5) Expect multi-modal data (PDFs, audio, images, spreadsheets) to be transmitted to CellCog’s service—review their privacy/terms and credits/costs. If you need stronger guarantees, limit file inputs, run tests with non-sensitive data, and audit network activity during initial use.
